g.text: Count the full cost of accepted work
A smaller prompt or cheaper model is valuable only when the complete, reviewed job improves.
Credit Karma’s Artifactory example motivates a paired
quality test. It does not establish equal answers or a
A reviewer’s correction, candidate selection and investigation time belong in the comparison. Include abandoned
runs and retries in cost even when only one final output is accepted. Report accepted-task rate beside unit cost
so narrower coverage cannot masquerade as improvement. Jellyfish’s salary-plus-AI framing and Ramp’s narrow
specialist work both shift attention to end-to-end economics. Separate prefill, generation, tool and human
delays. A smaller prompt or model can improve a stage while leaving total delivery time or quality worse.
Sources: Intuit Credit Karma · Jellyfish · Ramp | Reviewed October 25, 2026
